subject: Eval technical recap + bespoke benchmark instructions
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Rojas <emily@careline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval technical recap + bespoke benchmark instructions

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and an ops-first plan to get Careline’s classifier and triage assistant evaluated on Redwood. I’ve kept action items tight so we can get a pilot run in your staging environment by next week.

Call highlights (short):
- Goal: measure model fit for triage suggestions and diagnostic summarization; primary guardrail is hallucination rate and clinical correctness.
- Data shape: you'll provide de-identified triage transcripts + gold labels for intent and disposition. We discussed a 1k-sample pilot (stratified by severity).
- Constraints: low latency target for inference (p95 < 450ms) and strict audit logging for each request.

Recommended models to try on initial run (order is intentional):
1) rwi-13b-chat-q4 — good balance of instruction-following and latency; recommended for first pass.
2) rwi-7b-chat-int8 — lower cost; try if throughput is a concern during parallel scoring.
3) open-gg-30b-sparse (if you want higher-recall on long-context summarization) — expect higher token cost and longer tail latency.

Benchmark artifacts I’m attaching and links below:
- careline_sample_prompts.csv (attached): 50 representative prompts with expected labels and edge-case flags.
- careline_eval_schema_v1.jsonl (attached): scoring harness format we use on Redwood. Schema fields: id, prompt, expected, scoring_type (exact_match|f1|human_review), tags.
- Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCarelineEval — includes a starter scoring notebook and a prompt bank.

Scoring & pass/fail criteria (pilot):
- Intent classification: micro F1 >= 0.88 on the 1k holdout.
- Triage suggestion: human-reviewed correctness >= 92% (sampled 200 cases).
- Hallucination/regression guardrail: label-based mismatch rate <= 3% and any high-severity hallucination triggers immediate rollback.

Ops notes for Redwood setup (what we’ll do):
- We’ll provision a private pilot workspace under your account and pin rwi-13b-chat-q4 for the run.
- Turn on prefix KV caching for the triage pipeline to reduce token cost on repeated contexts.
- We’ll enable request tracing and export per-token latency breakdowns to the shared Drive report.

Action items (owners):
- Emily / Careline: share 1k de-identified sample (CSV/JSONL) and confirm S3 or Drive upload location. (ETA: Tue 08/24)
- Ben Carter (cc’d): will coordinate the pilot run and allocate Redwood test capacity.
- Priyom Das (cc’d): will prepare the scoring harness and run smoke tests on 50 samples.
- Michael Grant: will upload the scoring notebook and test prompts to the shared Drive and create the HubSpot deal record.

Attachments: careline_sample_prompts.csv (50 rows), careline_eval_schema_v1.jsonl (schema + 10 example records).

If that looks right, we’ll queue the pilot for Wed/Thu next week and share a short runbook once your samples are uploaded.

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Emily Rojas <emily@careline.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval technical recap + bespoke benchmark instructions

Thanks Michael — that summary is super helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) We can get the 1k de-identified set ready by Tue 08/24, we’ll upload to an S3 bucket (I’ll share credentials).
2) For the human review pass, can Redwood provide a short template for the reviewer checklist (we’ll use our clinicians for the 200-sample human check)?
3) Compliance: we are SOC 2 in-flight — can you confirm logging retention for the pilot (14 days vs 90 days)? We’d prefer 30 days if possible.

On models: Emily (careline) question — what’s the expected perf delta between rwi-13b-chat-q4 and rwi-7b-chat-int8 for intent F1? If the difference is small we may start with 7b for cost reasons.

I’ll share the S3 path and a sample of the CSV by EOD Monday. Looking forward to the runbook.

Best,
Emily

--
Emily Rojas
Head of Product, Careline Health
emily@careline.health | (617) 555-0134
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Rojas <emily@careline.health>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Eval technical recap + bespoke benchmark instructions — internal ops plan

Ben / Priyom — forwarding Emily’s reply and the plan. Quick internal game plan: 

- Ben: please provision the private pilot workspace under deal RWI-8421 and reserve 2x low-latency nodes (target p95 < 450ms). Start with rwi-13b-chat-q4 but be ready to spin the 7b-int8 variant if cost pressure shows up. Keep me posted on ETA for capacity.
- Priyom: please prepare the scoring harness so it accepts both CSV and JSONL and supports the attached schema. Include scripts to compute micro-F1, per-class precision/recall, and a simple hallucination detection flag (keyword + divergence heuristic). We’ll do the 50-sample smoke run first, then the 1k run.
- Compliance/log retention: Emily asked about retention windows. Priyom, can we support 30-day log retention for pilot? If it requires product/SLA exceptions, flag it and I’ll escalate.

Priyom, Ben — timeline: smoke run on Mon 08/23 (50 samples) and the full 1k run Wed 08/25 if samples arrive Tue. Please add concrete owner tasks in the shared Drive runbook I created and ping me when the pilot workspace is provisioned.

Emily — cc’ing our ops leads so we can be transparent on timing. If you want to swap the initial model to the 7b-int8, we can do that but I recommend starting with 13b to set the quality baseline (we’ll measure cost delta and can switch).

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
